instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Insert a single row with recipient='John'
output: INSERT INTO emails (recipient, status) VALUES ('John', 100);

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Insert multiple rows at once
output: INSERT INTO emails (recipient, status) VALUES ('John', 1), ('Jane', 2), ('Jim', 3);

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Insert into emails from a select that filters sent_at
output: INSERT INTO emails (recipient, status) SELECT recipient, status FROM emails_src WHERE sent_at = 'x';

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Update the row with id=7
output: UPDATE emails SET recipient = 'NewName' WHERE id = 7;

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Update all rows setting status to 0
output: UPDATE emails SET status = 0;

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Update emails increasing all status by 10%
output: UPDATE emails SET status = status * 1.1;

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Update rows where sent_at equals 'done'
output: UPDATE emails SET recipient = 'Finished' WHERE sent_at = 'done';

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Delete a row by id 12
output: DELETE FROM emails WHERE id = 12;

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Delete rows where status is below 50
output: DELETE FROM emails WHERE status < 50;

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Delete rows where sent_at is NULL
output: DELETE FROM emails WHERE sent_at IS NULL;

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Delete all rows from emails
output: DELETE FROM emails;

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Upsert: insert or update on conflict of the id
output: INSERT INTO emails (id, recipient) VALUES (1, 'X') ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET recipient = EXCLUDED.recipient;

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Conditional update using CASE
output: UPDATE emails SET status = CASE WHEN status > 100 THEN status - 10 ELSE status + 10 END;

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Update a join-based target using a subquery value
output: UPDATE emails SET status = (SELECT MAX(status) FROM emails) WHERE status IS NULL;

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Delete with a subquery filter
output: DELETE FROM emails WHERE status IN (SELECT status FROM emails WHERE sent_at = 'skip');

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Insert with explicit column list and defaults
output: INSERT INTO emails (recipient, status, sent_at) VALUES ('A', 5, 'active');

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Update with a LIMIT to only change a few rows
output: UPDATE emails SET status = status + 1 WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM emails LIMIT 5);

instruction:

Insert ignoring duplicates
output: INSERT OR IGNORE INTO emails (recipient) VALUES ('Dup');

instruction:
Schema: emails(id, recipient, status, sent_at)
Delete a range where status between two values
output: DELETE FROM emails WHERE status BETWEEN 20 AND 30;

instruction:

Update setting multiple columns
output: UPDATE emails SET recipient = 'Z', status = 0, sent_at = NULL WHERE id = 9;

instruction:

Insert a row returning its id
output: INSERT INTO emails (recipient) VALUES ('Ret') RETURNING id;

instruction:

Replace all occurrences in a string column
output: UPDATE emails SET sent_at = REPLACE(sent_at, 'a', 'b');

instruction:

Trim whitespace then update recipient
output: UPDATE emails SET recipient = TRIM(recipient);

instruction:

Lowercase a text column in place
